(F) NATURAL-LANGUAGE HYPOTHESIS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Summed social capital (ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument) peaked in the 14th century BCE (1400–1301
BCE; CE −1400..−1301), in the middle of the OBA cultural period. The peak value of the
3-component summed index is +4.24 (relative to a per-component z-score baseline of μ≈0, σ≈1
across 3,601 per-year Z records spanning 4100–500 BCE). The peak is robust under three of four
sensitivity variants — mean-of-12, clipped-negative SC3, and the default *_inter sum all
select K=14; only the raw-Z-at-bin-center variant breaks the strict tie between K=14 and
K=13 by returning K=13, an artifact of the warmer Amber (Zamber) tied at −0.01 across the two
bins and of the linear interpolation’s smoothing across them.

The 14th-century BCE capital peak is driven primarily by Copper+Gold (ZCU_AU = +2.54, the
all-time high for that series) and Monument Count (ZMonument = +1.71, top-3 of its series),
with Amber essentially flat at its long-run baseline (Zamber = −0.01, NOT rising into the
peak; it in fact declines monotonically from K=15 through K=12, from −0.08 → −0.01 →
−0.29 → −0.58). Beyond the SC3 trio, two further individual social-capital components
clearly RISE INTO this peak: HatchetSword (ZAxtSchwert = +2.61; second-highest in its 37-bin
record, top-3 series) and Dagger (ZDolch = +1.68; rank-3 in its series). MonumentSize
(ZMW = +0.64) also qualifies on the dual criterion (above long-run mean AND top-3 of its
series), and so the peak is a coherent weaponry-and-monumentality spike — high-value bronze
tools (HatchetSword, Dagger) and high monument counts/sizes occur simultaneously with
concentrated copper/gold deposition. The remaining components (HouseSize, Depot, Sickle,
AxesCelts, PotteryForm, PotteryDecoration) are decisively NOT co-peaking: most are below
their long-run means and the rest fail the top-3-of-series test.

Supporting demographic evidence from pollen_inter_100 (Belau/Woserin PC1 mean, 100-year
rolling) places the 14th-century BCE bin at +1.48 (rolling mean, positive regime) and the
adjacent 13th-century BCE bin at +2.04 — i.e., openness is high and rising through the OBA
peak, but pollen is itself still climbing toward its all-time window maximum in the latest
centuries (~+8.7 in the 6th–5th century BCE), so it is a corroborating rather than a
co-locating signal.

BOTTOM LINE:  In the 14th century BCE (1400–1301 BCE), summed social capital reached its peak
of +4.24 in the data window (4100–500 BCE); this peak is driven by Copper+Gold and
Monument Count within the SC3 trio, plus a wider cluster of rising individual components —
HatchetSword (+2.61), Dagger (+1.68), MonumentSize (+0.64) — representing a clear Bronze-Age
(OBA) co-spike of precious-metal deposition, monumental construction, and high-value bronze
weaponry.
